r3_status.G-12: OPEN: per-version configuration paths preserve old versions only if nobody edits an existing file, but r4 defines no enforcement or config-tree identity; compare still loads the current pathname, so a committed in-place edit can change archived eligibility and proposal evaluation.
r3_status.G-13: OPEN: the dirty fallback is removed, but `git status --porcelain -- <case-dir>` does not report ignored files; provisioning copies seed contents from the working tree, so ignored case files can affect a run without appearing in caseTree.

findings.claim: The case immutability check can certify a caseTree that does not identify all provisioned bytes. Ignored files under the case seed are absent from both the Git tree and ordinary porcelain status, while provisioning copies the working-tree seed recursively.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:50-56 specifies `git status --porcelain -- <dir>` and a HEAD tree; benchmark/provision.sh:202-209 walks every seed entry and benchmark/provision.sh:403-408 copies the working-tree seed with `cp -R`.
findings.fix: Provision committed case bytes from the recorded Git tree, or refuse modified, untracked, and ignored entries beneath the case directory using an explicit complete check. Add a fixture with an ignored file inside seed/ and prove it cannot enter a run.

findings.claim: Configuration-version immutability remains conventional rather than enforceable. Editing and committing `configurations/<id>/<version>.json` in place leaves the same pair identity, and no configTree joins the evidence; archived proposal eligibility can consequently be evaluated using different configuration content.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:64-67 calls per-version files immutable; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:86-91 includes sealed roster and fences but no configuration-tree identity; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:191-195 directs compare to load the current version pathname. Current analogous eligibility lookup reads installed content at benchmark/compare.py:533-544.
findings.fix: Either enforce append-only configuration versions against Git history in validate-kit, or record a configuration tree/blob object and load eligibility from the recorded commit/blob. Fixture an archived comparison after an attempted same-version edit.

findings.claim: The projection table still omits a current manifest key: `roster.independenceReason`. An implementer cannot tell whether it belongs in configuration notes, must be preserved verbatim, or is intentionally retired.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-2d-og/manifest.json:322 contains `roster.independenceReason`; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:136 enumerates roster-owned fields without it, and metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:147 repeats only delegateRoles and independence.
findings.fix: Project `roster.independenceReason` into a named configuration field and state its output, or explicitly retire it and include that loss among the equivalence exclusions.

findings.claim: The promised byte-equivalence test is internally inconsistent about titles. The join deliberately changes contract Intent to `<case.title> — <config.title>` and §5 permits title differences, but migration permits only ids, tag, and paths; therefore the required six-alias comparison cannot be implemented with one defined normalization set.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:130 makes title a permitted difference; benchmark/provision.sh:561-566 shows title is emitted into contract bytes; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:226-228 lists only ids, tag, and paths as equivalence differences.
findings.fix: Choose one contract: reproduce every legacy title byte-for-byte from case plus configuration fields, or add title/Intent explicitly to the normative difference list and acceptance fixture.

findings.claim: The instrument tag is not length-safe as claimed. `caseId` is bounded, but `caseVersion` has only a structural regex and can be arbitrarily long, so the generated tag can exceed filesystem or Git ref-component limits. The sealed SHA-256 over instrument bytes otherwise avoids line-ending/gofmt ambiguity because it hashes the actual copied bytes.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:185-190 defines the tag and claims it is short while giving no caseVersion length bound; current provisioning creates and pushes the tag at benchmark/provision.sh:536 and benchmark/provision.sh:631-632.
findings.fix: Add a bounded caseVersion length compatible with directory components and the complete ref, and validate the final ref with `git check-ref-format refs/tags/<tag>` before provisioning.

findings.claim: Acceptance still requires unspecified `immutability digests` even though r4 explicitly rejected an embedded case digest in favor of caseTree. This can cause an implementer to reintroduce the self-referential digest mechanism removed after G-4/G-8.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:48-56 rejects the self-referential digest and defines caseTree instead; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:277-279 nevertheless requires `immutability digests recorded and checked`.
findings.fix: Replace the acceptance phrase with explicit caseTree recording plus the complete committed-subtree/refusal checks. Do not add another embedded digest.

summary: R4 closes the pinning contradiction, correctly treats the three no-gain-5 configurations as warnings and unsealable rather than refusing their aliases, includes caseTree in both comparability and record agreement, and gives configuration versions stable paths. Mission id = caseId causes no current grammar, fence-key, contract-name, or runner-path collision because each cohort repetition has a separate target, and refusing unpinned cohort versions is the safe rule. Revision is still required because ignored working-tree bytes evade caseTree, configuration immutability is unenforced, one manifest key is unprojected, title equivalence is contradictory, tag length is not actually bounded, and acceptance accidentally resurrects an unspecified digest. Section 10 is broad enough for ordinary another-machine authoring once these missing validation rules are documented; no additional architectural object is needed.
